text:
Consider the relation $R$ on the set $\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$ defined by $(a,b)\in R$ if and only if $1+ab>0$. Then, among the statements :

I. The number of elements in R is 17

II. R is an equivalence relation
options: Both I and II are true
Neither I nor II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
On $S=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$, $1+ab>0⟺ab>-1⟺ab\geq 0$, since $ab$ is an integer.

Pairs with $ab\geq 0$: those with $a=0$ or $b=0$ number $5+5-1=9$; pairs of nonzero elements of the same sign number $2\times 2+2\times 2=8$. So $R$ has $9+8=17$ elements and statement I is true.

$R$ is reflexive ($a^{2}\geq 0$) and symmetric ($ab=ba$). However, $(2,0)\in R$ and $(0,-2)\in R$, while $2\times (-2)=-4<0$ gives $(2,-2)\notin R$. So $R$ is not transitive, not an equivalence relation, and statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

solution.body:

$b^{2}=a^{2}-a^{2}e^{2}=20-10=10\Rightarrow b=\sqrt{10}$

The centre of the ellipse is the midpoint of $S_{1}S_{2}$, that is $(4,8)$.

The first equation is the circle with centre $(4,8)$ and radius $\sqrt{10}$, equal to the semi-minor axis $b$ of the ellipse.

Every point of the ellipse is at a distance of at least $b$ from its centre, with equality only at the two ends of the minor axis, so the circle meets the ellipse at exactly these two points.

text:
If the system of linear equations :

$\begin{array}{l} x+y+z=6 \\ x+2y+5z=10 \\ 2x+3y+λz=μ \end{array}$

has infinitely many solutions, then the value of $λ+μ$ equals:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the condition for infinitely many solutions, we first calculate the determinant $D$ of the coefficients of $x,y,z$:

$D=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & λ \end{array}\right |=λ-6$

For infinitely many solutions, $D=0$.  

So, $λ-6=0\Rightarrow λ=6.$

Now, let us find $D_{1}$, the determinant obtained by replacing the first column with the constants:

$D_{1}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 10 & 2 & 5 \\ μ & 3 & λ \end{array}\right |=2λ+3μ-60$

Next, the determinant $D_{2}$ is obtained by replacing the second column with the constants:

$D_{2}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 1 & 10 & 5 \\ 2 & μ & λ \end{array}\right |=4(λ-μ+10)$

Finally, $D_{3}$ is obtained by replacing the third column with the constants:

$D_{3}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 2 & 10 \\ 2 & 3 & μ \end{array}\right |=μ-16$

For the system to have infinitely many solutions, all the determinants must be zero:

$D=D_{1}=D_{2}=D_{3}=0$

Substitute $λ=6$:

From $D_{3}=0$,  

$μ-16=0\Rightarrow μ=16.$

Thus,

$λ+μ=6+16=22$

text: Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} α & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 \end{array}\right ]$ and $B=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -5α & 0 \\ 0 & 4α & -2α \end{array}\right ]+\mathrm{adj}(A)$. If $\det (B)=66$, then $\det (\mathrm{adj}(A))$ equals :

solution.body:
Given $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} α & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 \end{array}\right ]$,

$|A|=α(15-0)-1(10-0)+2(8-0)=15α+6.$

From the cofactors of $A$,

$\mathrm{adj}A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 15 & 3 & -6 \\ -10 & 5α & 4 \\ 8 & -4α & 3α-2 \end{array}\right ],$

so

$B=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -5α & 0 \\ 0 & 4α & -2α \end{array}\right ]+\mathrm{adj}A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 16 & 3 & -6 \\ -10 & 0 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & α-2 \end{array}\right ].$

Expanding along the second column, whose only non-zero entry is $3$:

$|B|=-3\left |\begin{array}{ll} -10 & 4 \\ 8 & α-2 \end{array}\right |=-3(-10α+20-32)=30α+36.$

$30α+36=66\Rightarrow α=1$, so $|A|=15+6=21$.

For a $3\times 3$ matrix, $|\mathrm{adj}A|=|A|^{2}=21^{2}=441$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: Let $α=3+4+8+9+13+14+\ldots$ upto 40 terms. If $(\tan β)^{\frac{α}{1020}}$ is a root of the equation $x^{2}+x-2=0,β\in \left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$, then $\sin ^{2}β+3\cos ^{2}β$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
1. A series sum is defined : $𝜶=3+4+8+9+13+14+\ldots ..𝒕_{40}$

2. $(\tan 𝜷)^{\frac{α}{1020}}$ is a root of the quadratic equation $𝒙^{2}+𝒙-2=0$ where $𝜷\in \left (0,\frac{𝝅}{2}\right )$

3. To evaluate the expression $\sin ^{2}β+3\cos ^{2}β$

$\therefore$ $𝜶=3+4+8+9+13+14+\ldots ..𝒕_{40}$

$=7+17+27+\ldots ..+𝑻_{20}$

$=\frac{20}{2}\{(2)\cdot (7)+(20-1)\cdot (10)\}$

$=(10)\cdot (14+190)=2,040\ldots \ldots (𝒊)$

Equation (i) gives the value of $α=2,040$ :

$(\tan β)^{\frac{α}{1020}}=(\tan β)^{\frac{2040}{1020}}=\tan ^{2}β\ldots \ldots (ii)$

Now let us solve the quadratic equation $x^{2}+x-2=0$ :

$x^{2}+x-2=0\Rightarrow x^{2}+2x-x-2=0\Rightarrow (x+2)(x-1)=0$

$\Rightarrow \begin{array}{ll} p & q \\ -2 & 1 \end{array}$

where $𝒑$ and $𝒒$ are the roots

We have derived in equation $(ii)(\tan β)^{\frac{α}{1020}}=\tan ^{2}β$ which is also a root of the equation $x^{2}+x-2=0$ :

From the pair of roots we get  $\tan ^{2}β$ =1$\Rightarrow \tan β=\pm 1$ As $\tan ^{2}β⩾0$ always

$𝜷\in \left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )\Rightarrow \tan 𝜷=1\Rightarrow 𝜷=\frac{π}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \sin ^{2}β+3\cos ^{2}β=\sin ^{2}\frac{π}{4}+3\cos ^{2}\frac{π}{4}=\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )+\left (\frac{3}{2}\right )=2$

text: A candidate has to go to the examination centre to appear in an examination. The candidate uses only one means of transportation for the entire distance out of bus, scooter and car. The probabilities of the candidate going by bus, scooter and car, respectively, are $\frac{2}{5},\frac{1}{5}$ and $\frac{2}{5}$. The probabilities that the candidate reaches late at the examination centre are $\frac{1}{5},\frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{1}{4}$ if the candidate uses bus, scooter and car, respectively. Given that the candidate reached late at the examination centre, the probability that the candidate travelled by bus is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $B,S,C$ be the events of travelling by bus, scooter and car, and $L$ the event of reaching late. Given $P(B)=\dfrac{2}{5},P(S)=\dfrac{1}{5},P(C)=\dfrac{2}{5}$ and $P(L|B)=\dfrac{1}{5},P(L|S)=\dfrac{1}{3},P(L|C)=\dfrac{1}{4}$.

By the total probability theorem,

$P(L)=\frac{2}{5}\cdot \frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{5}\cdot \frac{1}{3}+\frac{2}{5}\cdot \frac{1}{4}=\frac{2}{25}+\frac{1}{15}+\frac{1}{10}=\frac{12+10+15}{150}=\frac{37}{150}.$

By Bayes' theorem,

$P(B|L)=\frac{P(B)P(L|B)}{P(L)}=\frac{\frac{12}{150}}{\frac{37}{150}}=\frac{12}{37}.$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{llllllllllllll} \text{Observation} & 𝒙_{1} & 𝒙_{2} & 𝒙_{3} & 𝒙_{4} & 𝒏 & \text{Observation} & 𝒚_{1} & 𝒚_{2} & 𝒚_{3} & 𝒚_{4} & 𝒚_{5} & 𝒚_{6} & 𝒏 \\ \text{Set} & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 4 & \text{Set} & 2 & 2 & 2 & 2 & 2 & 2 & 6 \end{array}$

$\text{Set}1⇉μ_{x}=\frac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{4}x_{i}}{4}=1\ldots .(i)$

$σ_{x}^{2}=\left [⎛⎝⎜\frac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{4}x_{i}^{2}}{4}⎞⎠⎟-μ_{x}^{2}\right ]=13\ldots \ldots (ii)$

Set $2⇉μ_{y}=\frac{\sum\limits _{j=1}^{6}y_{j}}{6}=2\ldots \ldots (iii)$

$σ_{y}^{2}=\left [⎛⎝⎜\frac{\sum\limits _{j=1}^{6}y_{j}^{2}}{6}⎞⎠⎟-μ_{y}^{2}\right ]=1\ldots \ldots (iv)$

We mathematically extract from equations $(i)$ and $(ii)$ :

$\sum\limits _{i=1}^{4}x_{i}=4\ldots .(𝒗)\sum\limits _{i=1}^{4}x_{i}^{2}=4\left (μ_{x}^{2}+13\right )=4(1+13)=56\ldots \ldots (𝒗𝒊)$

We mathematically extract from equations (iii) and (iv) :

$\sum\limits _{j=1}^{6}𝒚_{j}=12\ldots .(𝒗𝒊𝒊)\sum\limits _{j=1}^{6}y_{j}^{2}=6\left (𝝁_{y}^{2}+1\right )=6(4+1)=30\ldots \ldots (𝒗𝒊𝒊𝒊)$

We have mathematically compiled a summary of all the information in equations (v) through (viii) to compute the mean and the variance for the 10 datapoints in set $1\cup$ set 2 :

$μ_{t}=\frac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{4}x_{i}+\sum\limits _{j=1}^{6}y_{j}}{4+6}=\frac{4+12}{10}=1.6\ldots ..(𝒊𝒙)$

$σ_{t}^{2}=\left [\left (\frac{\sum _{i=1}^{4}𝒙_{i}^{2}+\sum _{j=1}^{6}𝒚_{j}^{2}}{4+6}\right )-𝝁_{t}^{2}\right ]$

$=\frac{56+30}{4+6}-\begin{array}{l} (1.6)^{2} \end{array}$

$=8.6-2.56=6.04$

text: If a straight line drawn through the point of intersection of the lines $4x+3y-1=0$ and $3x+4y-1=0$, meets the co-ordinate axes at the points P and Q , then the locus of the mid point of PQ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
[IMG]


1. A straight line $𝑳$ passes through the point of intersection of 2 straight lines: $\left \{\begin{array}{l} 𝑳_{1}:4𝒙+3𝒚-1=0 \\ 𝑳_{2}:3𝒙+4𝒚-1=0 \end{array} \right.$

2. The straight line $𝑳$ cuts the axes at $𝑷$ and $𝑸$

3. To identify the locus of the mid-point of the segment $PQ$

The point of intersection of $𝑳_{1}$ and $𝑳_{2}$ is $𝑰(𝜶,𝜷)$

The mid-point of the segment $𝑷𝑸$ is $𝑴(𝒉,𝒌)$

Analytical Study :

We first solve the pair of straight lines $𝑳_{1}$ and $𝑳_{2}$ to locate the point of intersection :

$\begin{array}{l} 4x+3y-1=0\Rightarrow 12x+9y=3 \\ 3x+4y-1=0\Rightarrow 12x+16y=4 \end{array}\Rightarrow β=\frac{1}{7}\Rightarrow 𝜶=\frac{1}{7}\Rightarrow 𝑰\left (\frac{1}{7},\frac{1}{7}\right )\ldots ..(i)$

The straight line $𝑳$ passes through the point $𝑰$ identified by equation (i)

The equation of the straight line $𝑳$ in point slope form is written below :

$L:\left (y-\frac{1}{7}\right )=m\left (x-\frac{1}{7}\right )\equiv L:7mx-7y=m-1\equiv L:\frac{7mx}{m-1}+\frac{7y}{1-m}=1\ldots .(ii)$

The equation (ii) gives the straight line $𝑳$ in intercept form where the $𝑿$ and $𝒀$ intercepts are observed below :

$\begin{array}{lll} \begin{array}{ll} 𝑷 & 𝑸 \\ \left (\frac{𝒎-1}{7𝒎},0\right ) & \left (0,\frac{1-𝒎}{7}\right ) \end{array}\text{..... Chart}1 \end{array}$
From Chart 1, the mid-point of the section $𝑷𝑸$ is derived applying mid-point formulae :

$M(h,k)=M\left (\frac{m-1}{14m},\frac{1-m}{14}\right )\equiv \begin{array}{lll} \text{Point} & h & k \\ M(h,k) & \frac{m-1}{14m} & \frac{1-m}{14} \end{array}\ldots .\text{Chart}2$
Chart 2 has the $𝑿$ and $𝒀$ coordinate each as a function of $𝒎$ where we can eliminate $𝒎$ and mathematically trace the locus :

$𝒌=\frac{1-𝒎}{14}\Rightarrow 𝒎=1-14𝒌\Rightarrow 𝒉=\frac{1-14𝒌-1}{14(1-14𝒌)}=\frac{14𝒌}{14(14𝒌-1)}=\frac{𝒌}{(14𝒌-1)}\Rightarrow 14𝒉𝒌-𝒉=𝒌\Rightarrow 𝒉+𝒌-14𝒉𝒌=0$

The locus of the mid-point of the section $𝑷𝑸$ after replacement of the dummy variables is found to be the rectangular hyperbola $𝒙+𝒚-14𝒙𝒚=0$

text:
Let $α=3\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{6}{11}\right )$ and $β=3\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{4}{9}\right )$, where inverse trigonometric functions take only the principal values.

Given below are two statements :

Statement I : $\cos (α+β)>0$.

Statement II : $\cos (α)<0$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\dfrac{1}{2}<\dfrac{6}{11}<\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $\sin ^{-1}$ is increasing, $\dfrac{π}{6}<\sin ^{-1}\dfrac{6}{11}<\dfrac{π}{4}$, so

$\frac{π}{2}<α<\frac{3π}{4}$

Thus $α$ lies in the second quadrant and $\cos α<0$, so Statement II is true.

Since $0<\dfrac{4}{9}<\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\cos ^{-1}$ is decreasing, $\dfrac{π}{3}<\cos ^{-1}\dfrac{4}{9}<\dfrac{π}{2}$, so

$π<β<\frac{3π}{2}$

Adding, $\dfrac{3π}{2}<α+β<\dfrac{9π}{4}$. Cosine is positive on $\left (\dfrac{3π}{2},\dfrac{5π}{2}\right )$, which contains this interval, so $\cos (α+β)>0$ and Statement I is true.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
For the function $f(x)=\mathrm{e}^{\sin |x|}-|x|,x\in 𝐑$, consider the following statements :

Statement I : $f$ is differentiable for all $x\in 𝐑$.

Statement II : $f$ is increasing in $\left (-π,-\frac{π}{2}\right )$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $x>0$, $f(x)=e^{\sin x}-x$ and $f^{'}(x)=e^{\sin x}\cos x-1$, so $f^{'}(0^{+})=1-1=0$.

For $x<0$, $f(x)=e^{-\sin x}+x$ and $f^{'}(x)=1-e^{-\sin x}\cos x$, so $f^{'}(0^{-})=1-1=0$.

Both one-sided derivatives at $x=0$ equal 0 and $f$ is differentiable at every $x\neq 0$, so $f$ is differentiable on $𝐑$; Statement I is true.

For $x\in \left (-π,-\dfrac{π}{2}\right )$, $\cos x<0$, so $f^{'}(x)=1-e^{-\sin x}\cos x>1>0$ and $f$ is increasing there; Statement II is true.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

Let $\vec{\mathrm{a}}=4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k},\mathrm{b}\leftarrow =10\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and a vector $\vec{\mathrm{c}}$ be such that $2(\vec{\mathrm{a}}\times \vec{\mathrm{b}})+3(\mathrm{b}\leftarrow \times \vec{\mathrm{c}})=\vec{0}$.

If $\vec{\mathrm{a}}\cdot \vec{\mathrm{c}}=15$, then $\vec{\mathrm{c}}\cdot (\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k})$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The unknown vector $\vec{𝒄}$ is represented in 3D: $\vec{𝒄}=𝒙\hat{𝒊}+𝒚\hat{𝒋}+z\hat{𝒌}$

Cross product of 2 vectors $\vec{𝒂}$ and $\vec{𝒃}$ :

$(\vec{𝒂}\times \vec{𝒃})=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{𝒊} & \hat{𝒋} & \hat{𝒌} \\ 4 & -1 & 3 \\ 10 & 2 & -1 \end{array}\right |=-5\hat{𝒊}+34\hat{j}+18\hat{𝒌}\ldots ..(i)$

Cross product of 2 vectors $\vec{𝒃}$ and $\vec{𝒄}$ :

$(\vec{𝒃}\times \vec{𝒄})=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 10 & 2 & -1 \\ 𝒙 & 𝒚 & 𝒛 \end{array}\right |=(2z+y)\hat{𝒊}-(10z+𝒙)\hat{𝒋}+(10𝒚-2𝒙)\hat{𝒌}\ldots \ldots (𝒊𝒊)$

We know, $2(𝒂\times 𝒃)+3(𝒃\times 𝒄)=0$

Dividing by $x\sqrt{1-x^{2}}dx$:

The integrating factor is $e^{\int \frac{dx}{x}}=x$, so

Integrating by parts with $\cos ^{-1}x$ as the first function and $\int \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}dx=-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$:

$xy=-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\cos ^{-1}x-\int \left (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\right )\left (-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right )dx=-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\cos ^{-1}x-x+C$

As $x\to 1^{-}$, $\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\cos ^{-1}x\to 0$, so $\lim _{x\to 1^{-}}y=C-1=1$, giving $C=2$.

$y\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=3-\frac{π}{\sqrt{3}}$

text: Let $\frac{x^{2}}{f(a^{2}+7a+3)}+\frac{y^{2}}{f(3a+15)}=1$ represent an ellipse with major axis along $y$-axis, where $f$ is a strictly decreasing positive function on $𝐑$. If the set of all possible values of $a$ is $𝐑-[α,β]$, then $α^{2}+β^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since the ellipse has its major axis along the $y$-axis, the denominator under $y^{2}$ must be bigger than the denominator under $x^{2}$.

So we need

$f(3a+15)>f\left (a^{2}+7a+3\right ).$

Given that $f$ is a strictly decreasing positive function, a bigger function value happens when the input is smaller. So,

$3a+15<a^{2}+7a+3.$

Bring all terms to one side:

$a^{2}+7a+3-3a-15>0$

$a^{2}+4a-12>0.$

Complete the square:

$a^{2}+4a-12=(a+2)^{2}-16.$

So the inequality becomes

$(a+2)^{2}-16>0\Rightarrow (a+2)^{2}>16.$

Taking square roots,

$|a+2|>4\Rightarrow a+2>4\text{or}a+2<-4.$

So,

$a>2\text{or}a<-6.$

That means the allowed values are

$a\in 𝐑-[-6,2].$

Hence, $α=-6$ and $β=2$. Therefore,

$α^{2}+β^{2}=(-6)^{2}+(2)^{2}=36+4=40.$

text:
The sum of squares of all the real solutions of the equation 

$\log _{(x+1)}\left (2x^{2}+5x+3\right )=4-\log _{(2x+3)}\left (x^{2}+2x+1\right )$ is equal to $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The bases need $x+1>0$, $x+1\neq 1$, $2x+3>0$, $2x+3\neq 1$, and the arguments $2x^{2}+5x+3=(x+1)(2x+3)$ and $x^{2}+2x+1=(x+1)^{2}$ must be positive. Together these give $x>-1$, $x\neq 0$.

Using the factorisations, the equation becomes

$1+\log _{(x+1)}(2x+3)=4-2\log _{(2x+3)}(x+1).$

Put $u=\log _{(x+1)}(2x+3)$, so that $\log _{(2x+3)}(x+1)=\dfrac{1}{u}$:

$1+u=4-\dfrac{2}{u}\Rightarrow u^{2}-3u+2=0\Rightarrow u=1\text{or}u=2.$

For $u=1$: $2x+3=x+1\Rightarrow x=-2$, which is rejected since $x>-1$.

For $u=2$: $2x+3=(x+1)^{2}\Rightarrow x^{2}=2\Rightarrow x=\pm \sqrt{2}$. Here $x=-\sqrt{2}<-1$ is rejected, while $x=\sqrt{2}$ satisfies every condition.

The only real solution is $x=\sqrt{2}$, so the sum of squares of the solutions is $(\sqrt{2})^{2}=2$.

Hence, the answer is 2.

text: Let $f$ be a polynomial function such that $\log _{2}(f(x))=\left (\log _{2}\left (2+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{9}+\ldots \ldots \infty \right )\right )\cdot \log _{3}\left (1+\frac{f(x)}{f(1/x)}\right ),x>0$ and $f(6)=37$. Then $\sum\limits _{\mathrm{n}=1}^{10}f(\mathrm{n})$ is equal to $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement of Work :

1. $𝒇(𝒙)$ is a polynomial function

2. A logarithmic equation involving function $\left. f:\log _{2}[f(x)]=\left [\log _{2}\left (2+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{9}+\ldots ..\infty \right )\right ]\cdot \log _{3}\left \{1+\frac{𝒇(𝒙)}{f\left (\frac{1}{𝒙}\right )}\right \}\right ];x>0$ and $𝒇(6)=37$

3. To evaluate the sum : $\sum\limits _{n=1}^{10}𝒇(n)$

$\left.  \left. \begin{array}{ll} \log _{2}[𝒇(𝒙)] & =\left [\log _{2}\left (2+\dfrac{2}{3}+\dfrac{2}{9}+\ldots .\infty \right )\right ]\cdot \left [\log _{3}\left \{1+\dfrac{𝒇(𝒙)}{𝒇\left (\frac{1}{𝒙}\right )}\right \}\right ] \\ =\left [\log _{2}2\left \{1+\dfrac{1}{3}+\left (\dfrac{1}{3}\right )^{2}+\ldots ..\infty \right \}\right ]\cdot \left |~\log _{3}\left \{1+\dfrac{𝒇(𝒙)}{𝒇\left (\frac{1}{𝒙}\right )}\right \}\right ]. \\ =\left [\log _{2}2\left (\dfrac{1}{1-\frac{1}{3}}\right )\right ]\cdot \left [\log _{3}\left \{1+\dfrac{𝒇(𝒙)}{𝒇\left (\frac{1}{𝒙}\right )}\right \}\right ] \\ =[\log _{2}3]\cdot \right |~\log _{3}\left \{1+\dfrac{𝒇(𝒙)}{𝒇\left (\frac{1}{𝒙}\right )}\right \}\right ] \end{array}$

$\frac{\log _{2}[f(x)]}{\log _{2}3}=\left [\log _{3}\left \{1+\frac{f(x)}{f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )}\right )\right ]$

$\Rightarrow \log _{3}[f(x)]=\log _{3}\left \{1+\frac{𝒇(𝒙)}{f\left (\frac{1}{𝒙}\right )}\right \}$

$\Rightarrow f(x)=1+\frac{f(x)}{f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )}$

$\Rightarrow$ $f(x)\cdot f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )=f(x)+f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )$ .....(i)

The function $𝒇(𝒙)$ is a polynomial function stated in SOW where $𝒇(6)=37=(6)^{2}+1\ldots ..(𝒊𝒊)$ 

Equation (ii) on logical analysis reduces the polynomial $𝒇(𝒙)$ to the possible form below : 

$f(x)=x^{2}+1\ldots \ldots (iii)\leftarrow$ Cubic powers of $x$ is not possible where $f(6)>216$ 

Now let us analyze the polynomial function $𝒇(𝒙)$ from preconditions set in SOW :

$f(x)\cdot f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )=\left (1+x^{2}\right )\cdot \left (1+\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right )=1+\frac{1}{x^{2}}+x^{2}+1=\left (1+x^{2}\right )+\left (1+\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right )=f(x)+f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )\ldots .(iv)$

Equation $(ii),(iii)$ and $(iv)$ mathematically certify the polynomial $f(x)=1+x^{2}$ :

$f(x)=1+x^{2}$

$\Rightarrow s_{10}=\sum\limits _{n=1}^{10}f(𝒏)=\sum\limits _{𝒏=1}^{10}\left (1+𝒏^{2}\right )=\sum\limits _{𝒏=1}^{10}(1)+\sum\limits _{n=1}^{10}\left (n^{2}\right )$

$=10+\frac{(10)\cdot (10+1)\cdot \{(2)\cdot (10)+1\}}{6}=10+385=395$
